items.title: Priority and accelerated grid connections
items.summary: Government policy says strategic demand projects and AI Growth Zones will be prioritised for available electricity-network capacity. Data-centre projects inside AI Growth Zones qualify for the Connections Accelerator Service.
items.claim_limit: This does not mean every data centre receives priority, and it does not prove that a particular project has received a connection.

items.status: Planned from April 2027, subject to implementation
items.title: Targeted electricity-price support
items.summary: Government policy proposes electricity-cost reductions for eligible AI Growth Zone data centres of up to £24/MWh in Scotland, £16/MWh in Cumbria and £14/MWh in the North East.
items.claim_limit: These are maximum policy figures for eligible projects, not evidence that a particular site is receiving a discount today.

items.scope: AI data centres / AI Growth Zones
items.title: Planning support and reduced barriers
items.summary: Government policy sets out planning reforms intended to prioritise AI data centres, streamline consent processes and protect land for AI Growth Zones.
items.claim_limit: Planning support is not the same as planning permission, and it does not prove a data-centre proposal takes priority over housing in an individual local decision.

items.status: Available for viable projects to explore
items.title: Public-sector finance can help unlock private investment
items.summary: Government policy says the National Wealth Fund and UK Export Finance will look to support the AI Growth Zone programme and explore viable data-centre projects within growth zones.
items.claim_limit: This is a programme-level commitment. It is not evidence that a named project has received public money unless a project-specific award is separately identified.

items.title: AI Growth Zones are designed around power and planning access
items.summary: The government's AI Growth Zone application material says the programme is intended to unlock AI-enabled data centres and supporting infrastructure by improving access to power and providing planning support.
items.claim_limit: A location appearing near a data centre does not automatically mean it is inside an AI Growth Zone. Grid Watch only labels individual sites as zone-linked when an open source explicitly supports that link.

items.title: Culham AI Growth Zone
items.summary: Government identified Culham in Oxfordshire as the first AI Growth Zone, centred on the UK Atomic Energy Authority campus and intended to accelerate AI data-centre development and supporting infrastructure.
items.claim_limit: The zone designation does not mean every mapped data centre within the wider Oxfordshire area receives every support mechanism.

items.scope: Blyth/Cambois and Cobalt Park, North East England
items.title: North East AI Growth Zone
items.summary: Government announced an AI Growth Zone anchored by sites around Blyth/Cambois in Northumberland and Cobalt Park in North Tyneside, with the aim of creating one of Europe's major data-centre hubs.
items.claim_limit: Regional designation is not proof that every nearby data-centre project receives direct public funding or a specific grid connection advantage.
items.source_label: GOV.UK — North East AI Growth Zone

items.title: North Wales AI Growth Zone
items.summary: Government announced a North Wales AI Growth Zone with potential links to future power infrastructure around Wylfa and large-scale AI data-centre development.
items.claim_limit: Potential future energy supply and zone status do not prove a particular nearby data centre is connected to Wylfa or has received a subsidy.
items.source_label: GOV.UK — North Wales AI Growth Zone

items.title: South Wales AI Growth Zone
items.summary: Government announced a South Wales AI Growth Zone including development at the former Ford Bridgend Engine Plant as part of a wider package of AI investment.
items.claim_limit: The announcement is regional/programme evidence and does not prove every nearby mapped site receives the same support.
items.source_label: GOV.UK — South Wales AI Growth Zone

items.title: Lanarkshire AI Growth Zone
items.summary: Government announced Lanarkshire as Scotland's AI Growth Zone. The announcement states the status remains conditional on delivery against agreed milestones and legal and regulatory requirements.
items.claim_limit: The government's jobs and investment figures for this zone were supplied by the developer; they are not an independent estimate of realised economic benefit.

items.title: Investment Zone tax reliefs
items.summary: Eligible businesses within designated Investment Zone tax sites can access reliefs including Business Rates, Stamp Duty Land Tax, Employer National Insurance Contributions, Enhanced Structures and Buildings Allowance and Enhanced Capital Allowances.
items.claim_limit: Being near an Investment Zone is not enough. Grid Watch must confirm that a project sits inside a designated tax-site boundary before presenting tax-site eligibility, and eligibility is still not proof that a business claimed a particular relief.

items.scope: Published UK Investment Zone tax sites
items.title: Official tax-site boundary maps exist
items.summary: HMRC publishes official maps for designated Investment Zone tax sites, including locations in the East Midlands, Flintshire and Wrexham, Glasgow City Region, Liverpool City Region, North East, North East of Scotland and West Midlands.
items.claim_limit: The map collection is evidence of designated tax areas; it is not evidence that a particular data centre occupies one until the site location is checked against the legal boundary.
